title: Bombay High Court Orders Breach Candy Swimming Bath Trust to Pay Rs 11.67 Lakh Gratuity to Ex-Manager
case_name: Breach Candy Swimming Bath Trust v. Rajesh Somnath Nerkar
card_summary: Justice Sandeep Marne dismissed Breach Candy Swimming Bath Trust's challenge to an order directing it to pay Rs 11.67 lakh gratuity, with interest, to its former manager of 23 years, plus Rs 1 lakh costs. The court held the Trust could not bypass the statutory appeal under the Gratuity Act by going straight to the High Court, rejecting its claim that an alleged loss justified withholding the gratuity.
card_tip: Skipping the statutory appeal under the Gratuity Act to go straight to a writ court invites both dismissal and costs; exhaust the forum the Act provides first.
verification_notes: Confirmed by Free Press Journal and Rawlaw; both agree on the gratuity amount, the Rs 1 lakh costs, the procedural ground for dismissal (bypassing statutory appeal), and the Trust's rejected Rs 5 crore loss defence. The two sources give different interest figures (10% vs 15% compound), so the specific rate is omitted from the card pending judgment text.
